One caveat not resolvable from the excerpt: Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures reflect a materially larger reporting entity than FY2023 following its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings (closed September 2024), so its revenue growth is not organic and is not like-for-like with the other four carriers. The excerpt provides no segment or pro-forma detail to isolate this, so treat Alaska's growth rank as inflated.

**Revenue growth, FY2023 → FY2024**

| Rank | Airline | FY2023 | FY2024 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Alaska | $10,426M | $11,735M | +12.6% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $53,717M | $57,063M | +6.2% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Delta | $58,048M | $61,643M | +6.2% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.3% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | American | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.7% [DOC-1] |

United (6.23%) and Delta (6.19%) are effectively tied, separated by ~4 basis points.

**Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ revenue)**

| Rank | Airline | Op. income | Revenue | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M | $61,643M | 9.7% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $5,096M | $57,063M | 8.9% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M | $11,735M | 4.9% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | American | $2,614M | $54,211M | 4.8% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M | $27,483M | 1.2% [DOC-1] |

Alaska (4.86%) and American (4.82%) are essentially tied.

**Is the top-ranked airline the same?** No. Alaska leads on revenue growth (+12.6%, aided by the Hawaiian acquisition), while Delta leads on FY2024 operating margin (9.7%). Delta ranks only 3rd on growth, and Alaska ranks 3rd on margin.

ANSWER: No — revenue growth ranking: Alaska (+12.6%), United (+6.2%), Delta (+6.2%), Southwest (+5.3%), American (+2.7%); FY2024 operating margin ranking: Delta (9.7%), United (8.9%), Alaska (4.9%), American (4.8%), Southwest (1.2%). Alaska tops growth (inflated by the Hawaiian acquisition), Delta tops margin.
